Standard ( Part 1 ) was Institution on 22 February 1983, after formers and Inductors for Electronics had been approved by the Electronics Council. 0.2 The object of this standard ( Part ments for the electrical, mechanical methods for frame output transformers

1 ) is to establish uniform requireand climatic properties and test used with television picture tubes. the

0.3 Detailed specification for the frame output transformers shall cover specific requirements and shall form other parts of this standard.

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of~a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2of significant places retained in the rounded off 1960*. The number value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) relates to general requirements and methods of test for judging the mechanical, electrical and environmental properties of frame output transformers primarily intended for use with television picture tubes.

2.2 Acceptance Tests - Tests carried out on frame output transformers selected from a lot which has passed the routine tests for the purpose of acceptance of the lot. 2.2.1 Lot - All frame output transformers and rating manufactured by the same factory the same process and materials. of the same type, category during the same period using

2.3 Type Tests - Tests carried out to prove conformity with the requirements of this standard. These are intended to prove the general qualities and design of a particular type of frame output transformer. 2.4 Type - A type comprises of products having similar functions manufactured by the same techniques and falling within the manufacturers usual range of ratings of these products.

2.5 Frame Output Transformer - A transformer with silicon steel magnetic circuit with primary, secondary and tertiary winding used as coupling element between the saw tooth current generator and the deflection coil. Tertiary winding can be used for voltage feed back. 3. TYPE DESIGNATION

The ambient temperature during the test shall be stated in the test report. 7.1;5 Other Precautions - During measurements the frame output transformer shall not be exposed to draughts, direct sun-rays or other influences likely to cause errors. 7.1.6 Test Frequency - When a test frequency is specified with no tolerance, the frequency used shall be within 1 percent of the specified value.

IS : 10488 ( Part 1 ) - 1983 7.3 General Tests

7.3.1 Visual Examination -- The frame output transformer shall be visually examined for workmanship, finish, condition and marking and these shall be satisfactory. 7.3.2 Dimensions - The dimensions shall be checked for compliance with those specified in the relevant specification and as per manufacturers drawings where the requirements are not covered. 7.4 Electrical Tests

7.4.1 Continuity of Windings - The windings of the frame output transformer shall be tested for electrical continuity by an suitable method. The wi.nding shall be continuous. 7.4.2 DC Resistance - The dc resistance shall be measured with a resistance bridge or other suitable test equipment. The test current through the specimen shall be as small as practical considering the sensitivity of the indicating instruments, unless the current or voltage is specified. When it is important that the temperature of the specimen shall not rise appreciably during the measurements, the test voltage shall be applied uninterruptedly for as short a time as practicable, but in no case for more than 5 seconds, unless otherwise specified. The measurement shall be made at or corrected to 25�C. The value shall be within the tolerance limits as specified. 7.4.3 a) Inductance The test shall be carried out as given below: inductance is to be 1 with an external frequency f 1 of the of the RF signal electronic voltmeter. to C's and the new inductance L of the

7.4.4 Transformation Ratio - The transformation ratio of the transformer shall be computed from the ratio of voltages measured across the required winding with the secondary open circuited and the measurement being done with a high impedance voltmeter.
7.4.5 Voltage Proof - Unless otherwise specified, the frame output transformer shall withstand without breakdown the application of an ac test voltage of the value shown as under: Maximum Working V 25 and below over 25 up to 50 over 50 up to 100 over 100 up to 175 over 175 up to 700 over 700 2.6 1.4 Voltage Test I'bltage V 50 100 300 500

IS : 10488 ( Part 1 ) - 1983 7.4.6 Insulation Resistance -.- Unless otherwise specified, the insulation resistance shall be measured by applying dc test voltages as mentioned below for one minute f 5 seconds between case and each winding and The voltage shall not be applied also between windings if applicable. gradually but shall be applied immediately through the internal resistance of the test apparatus. The insulation resistance shall be read after one minute & 5 seconds. 7.5 Temperature Rise - This test shall be carried out at a temperature not exceeding the upper category temperature. The frame output transformer shall be mounted so as to be protected from draughts and shall not be subjected to radiations from warmer objects. The thermometer ( which may be of thermocouple type ) used for measuring the ambient temperature shall be protected against trivial temperature changes. The frame output transformer shall be mounted in the monitor unit. The deflection current shall be adjusted for 5 percent overscan. The dc resistance of the line and frame coils shall be measured before the test at ambient temperature. Temperature rise will be determined by resistance measuring within 10 seconds after switching off the frame output transformer. A`i will be calculated from the formula:

IS:10488(Partl)-1983 7.6 Solderability - The frame output transformer provided with tag and lead type terminations shall I be subjected to the soldering iron test ( Method 3 ) with a soldering iron of suitable size in accordance with Set 1 of IS : 9000 ( Part XVIII )-1981*. At the end of the test, the component shall be visually examined. It shall not show any loosening of connections, melting or seepage of sealing materia1 or any other deterioration. The continuity of the winding shall be checked. 7.7 Robustness of Terminations

7.7.1 Tensile Test on all Terminations - All terminations shall be subjected to the test in accordance with Set 1 of IS : 9000 ( Part X1X)-1978*. The loading weight, the duration of the test and the number of bands shall be as specified in the relevant specification. In the case of pliable terminations, the bending test shall be carried out in accordance with Set 3 of IS : 9000 ( Part XIX )-1978*. 7.8 Bump - The frame output transformer shall be mounted as specified in Set 2 of IS : 9000 ( Part VII )-1979 *. Taking care that the terminations are not stressed and that equal number of samples are bumped in each of the three principal axes. Samples shall be subjected to 1 000 bumps at an acceleration of 250 m/sa, unless otherwise specified. After the test, the frame output transformer shall be visually examined and shall not show any damage or deterioration. The continuity of the winding shall be checked. 7.9 Vibration - The frame output transformer shall be mounted tested as required in IS : 9000 ( Part VIII )-1981* taking care that terminations are not stressed and that equal number of samples subjected to vibration test in each of the three principal axes. vibration severity should be 10 to 55 Hz with duration of six hours. and the are The

transformer shall be visually After the test, the frame output examined and there shall not be any damage or deterioration. The continuity of the winding shall be checked. The dc resistance and inductance shall be measured and should be within specified limits. Voltage proof test shall also be carried out. There shall be no change in insulation resistance when measured at the end of this test. *Basic environmental testing procedures for electronic and electrical items : Part VII Impact test, Set 2 Bump.

Part VIII Vibration. Part XVIII Solderability test, Set 1 Solderability of wire and tag terminations. Part XIX Test for robustness of terminations and integral mounting devices: Set 1 Tensile test Set 3 Bending test

IS : 10488 ( Part 7.10 Climatic Tests

1 ) - 1983

7.10.1 Climatic Sequence 7.10.2 Dry Heat - The frame output transformer shall be subjected to the dry heat test in accordance with Set 5 of IS : 9000 ( Part III )-1977*. The temperature of the test chamber shall be maintained at the maximum category temperature of the frame output transformer. The frame output transformer shall be on full load during exposure if specified in the relevant specification. While still at the high temperature and during the last half hour of exposure, the insulation resistance shall be measured and shall be not less than the value specified in the relevant specification. After recovery the frame output transformer shall be visually examined for any damage or deterioration. The insulation resistance shall be measured and it shall not deviate from the values obtained therein. 7.10.3 Dump Heat ( Cyclic ) ( First Cycles ) - The frame output transformer shall be subjected to the first cycle of this test in accordance with Set 2 of IS : 9000 ( Part V )-1981*. The duration of the recovery period shall be one and a half hours. After recovery, the frame output transformer shall be visually examined for any damage or deterioration. 7.10.4 Cold lest - The frame output transformer shall be sub.jected to the cold test in accordance with Set 4 of IS : 9000 ( Part II )-1977." The temperature of the chamber shall be maintained at the minimum category temperature. The duration of recovery period shall be one and a half After recovery the frame output transformer shall be visually hours. examined and there shall not be any damage or deterioration. The following tests shall be carried out: a) Continuity b) Voltage of the winding; and proof.

7.10.3 Air Pressure ( Lour ) - The frame output transformer shall be subjected to low air pressure test in accordance with IS : 90C0 ( Part XIII )1981%. The pressure shall be appropriate to the category and the duration shall be 5 minutes. During the period of exposure, a test voltage equal to 120 percent the working voltage shall be applied between terminals of the windings. of

Part III Dry heat test, Set 5 Dry heat for heat dissipating items with gradual change of temperatures. Part V Damp heat ( cyclic ) tests, Set 2 12 f 12 h cycle. Part XIII Low air pressure test.

After recovery of 24 hours the components shall be subjected to visual There shall not be examination and the continuity of winding is tested. any apparent damage or illegibility of marking and the windings shall be continuous. The frame output transformer shall then be subjected to dc resistance, inductance, voltage proof and insulation resistance tests. The values shall not be less than those specified in the relevant specification. 7.11 Damp Heat ( be subjected to the IS : 9000 ( Part IV accordance with the shall Steady State ) - The frame output transformer damp heat ( steady state ) test in accordance with The duration of the exposure shall be in )-1979*. category of the component under test.

After cleaning and recovery, the component shall be subjected to a visual examination and the continuity of windings There shall not be any apparent damage, the markings shall be tested. shall be legible and the windings shall be continuous.
*Basic Part Part Part tBasic electrical environmental testing procedures for electronic and electrical items: IV Damp heat ( steady state ) . V Damp heat ( cycle ) tests, Set 2 12+12 h cycle. X Mould growth test. climatic and mechanical durability tests for components for electronic equipment ( revised ).

and

14

IS : 10488 ( Part 1 ) - 1983 7.14 Shock - The frame output transformer shall be subjected to shock test in accordance with Set 1 of IS : 9000 ( Part VII )-1979*. At the end of the test the component shall be subjected to visual examination and the continuity of windings. There shall not be any apparent damage, the markings shall be legible and the windings shall be continuous. The frame output transformer shall then be subjected to dc resistance, inductance, voltage proof and insulation resistance tests. The values shall not be less than those specified in the relevant specification. 7.15 Acceleration - The frame output transformer shall be subjected to acceleration test in accordance with 7.7 of IS : 589-19617. At the end of this test the component shall be subjected to visual examination and the continuity of windings. There shall not be any apparent damage, the marking shall be legible and windings shall be continuous. The components shall then be subjected to dc resistance, inductance, voltage proof and insulation resistance tests. The values shall not be less than those specified in the relevant specification, 7.16 Endurance ( Electrical ) - The frame output transformer shall be mounted in accordance with the detail specification. Each winding shall be loaded with its rated current. The test shall be carried out at the maximum category temperature and the duration of this test shall be 1 000 hours, unless otherwise specified. At the end of 1 000 hours period, the frame output transformer shall be allowed to cool under standard atmospheric conditions for testing. The component shall then be subjected to visual examination and continuity of windings. There shall not be any apparent damage, the marking shall be legible and the winding shall be continuous. The frame output transformer shall further be subjected to dc resistance, inductance, voltage proof and insulation resistance tests. The values shall not be less than those specified, in the relevant specifications. 7.17 Flammability - The test shall be carried the procedure given in Appendix A. out in accordance with

7.17 )
TEST

FLAMMABILITY A-l. OBJECT
to determine

A-l.1 This test is intended will support combustion. A-2. TEST CHAMBER A-2.1 The chamber

whether

frame

output transformer

used for this test shall have the following

provisions: provided with supply of fresh

a) An enclosure protected from air currents, but means of venting fumes and admitting an adequate air at the bottom.

NOTE 1 - A metal box about 600 mm wide, 900 mm high and 600 mm deep, with a detachable front, a viewing window and suitable holes for intake of air and venting of fumes may be used. NOTE 2 - Adequate safety precautions possible explosion of the components. shall be taken to protect personnel from

b) A suitable stand or support for the frame involving a minimum of heat transfer; and c)

output

transformers

A spirit burner of the pattern shown in Fig. 2 or of a,ny other pattern. The fuel for the burner shall be good quality 66" OP industrial methylated spirit containing not more than 5 percent of wood naphtha ( see IS : 324-1959" ). The burner and the flame are considered satisfactory if a bare copper wire 0.71 mm dia having a free length of not less than 100 mm in the flame in the position to be occupied by frame output by transformer, melts in less than 6 seconds.
The melting point of copper is 1083�C.

NOTE -

A-3.

MOUNTING

A-3.1 The frame output transformer shall be mounted on the stand placed within the test chamber, in such a manner, that they are not shielded of the frame outfrom the flame by the support. Th e precise orientation put transformer relative to the flame, if not stated in the relevant specifications, shall be that judged to be the most unfavourable or which presents maximum surface to the test flame. *Specification for ordinary denatured spirit ( revised ).
